title: MS PowerPoint
summary: Slides, placeholders, views, slide master, transitions vs animations and the show-control keys (F5, Esc, B/W). PowerPoint questions are short-recall - mostly extensions, views and slideshow keys.

subtopics.title: Slides, placeholders and file types
subtopics.concept: **MS PowerPoint** is a presentation program. A file is a **presentation** made of **slides**. A slide holds text, pictures, tables and charts in boxes called **placeholders**. The **layout** decides where the boxes sit, and the **theme** decides colours and fonts.

tricks.title: Layout, theme, template
tricks.body: Layout arranges boxes. Theme sets colours and fonts. Template packages a theme and layouts in one file, .potx.

tricks.title: One change for all slides
tricks.body: To change all slides at once, edit the Slide Master on the View tab.

example.q: How can a logo be added to every slide in one step?
steps: A single slide controls all others.
That slide is the Slide Master.
Place the logo on the master.
example.answer: Add the logo on the Slide Master

mistakes.wrong: Calling a whole file a slide.
mistakes.right: The file is a presentation. A slide is one page of it.
A theme sets colours and fonts. A layout sets box positions.

mistakes.wrong: Adding the logo to each slide by hand.
mistakes.right: Place it once on the Slide Master.
.ppsx is a slide show. A template is .potx.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking handouts can hold any number of slides per page.
mistakes.right: Handouts hold 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 slides per page.

subtopics.notes:
### What PowerPoint is
PowerPoint is a **presentation** program from the Microsoft Office suite. It makes slide shows for classes, meetings and talks. A file is a **presentation**. It is made of **slides**.

### Parts of the window
| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Slide pane** | The large centre area where you edit one slide |
| **Thumbnail pane** | The left strip that lists all slides |
| **Notes pane** | The area below the slide for speaker notes |
| **Ribbon** | Tabs of commands |
| **Status bar** | Shows slide number and the view buttons |

The Ribbon tabs are **File, Home, Insert, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Review, View**.

### Slide parts
- A **placeholder** is a dotted box that holds a title, text, a picture or a chart.
- A **layout** is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide. Title Slide, Title and Content and Blank are layouts.
- A **theme** is a set of colours, fonts and effects for the whole deck. It is on the Design tab.
- A **template** is a saved file that carries a theme, layouts and sample content. Its extension is **.potx**.

> **Rule:** Layout is about where things sit. Theme is about how they look. Template is a saved package of both.

### Slide Master
The **Slide Master** is the top slide that controls every other slide. Change the font, logo or background on the master and all slides follow. It is on the View tab. Use it to put a logo on every slide in one step.

### What you can add to a slide
- Text boxes, shapes, pictures, clip art and icons.
- Tables, charts and **SmartArt** diagrams.
- Audio, video and screen recordings.
- Hyperlinks and **action buttons**. They jump to another slide or file.
- Header, footer, slide number and date.

### Files
| Extension | Type |
|---|---|
| **.pptx** | Default presentation from PowerPoint 2007 |
| **.ppt** | Old 97-2003 presentation |
| **.ppsx** | Slide show. It opens straight in show mode |
| **.potx** | Template |
| **.pptm** | Macro-enabled presentation |

> **Tip:** Double-click a .ppsx file and it opens directly as a slide show. A .pptx opens for editing.

### Working with slides
- **New Slide** adds a slide after the selected one. The key is Ctrl+M.
- **Duplicate Slide** copies the selected slide. The key is Ctrl+D.
- **Delete** removes the selected slide.
- **Sections** group slides under named headings in a long deck.
- **Reuse Slides** brings slides in from another file.

### Handouts and printing
A **handout** prints several slides on one page. The choices are **1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9** slides per page. The 3-slide layout adds lines for notes. A **Notes Page** prints one slide with its speaker notes below.

> **Note:** Speaker notes are seen by the speaker only. The audience does not see them.

patterns.name: Layout vs theme vs template
patterns.howToSpot: The question describes a job, such as setting colours, or arranging boxes, or saving a whole design.
steps: Arrangement of boxes is a layout.
Colours and fonts make up a theme.
A saved package of both is a template (.potx).
patterns.why: The three words sound alike, but each has one job.

example.q: The set of colours, fonts and effects applied to a whole presentation is called a:
steps: The set covers the whole deck.
It covers looks, not box positions.
That is a theme.

patterns.name: Slide Master
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks how to change all slides at once, or where the logo goes.
steps: Open the View tab and choose Slide Master.
Edit the font, logo or background on it.
All slides based on it follow.
patterns.why: One master controls the whole deck.

example.q: Which slide controls the look of all other slides?
steps: One top-level slide sets the look.
It is the Slide Master.

patterns.name: PowerPoint file extensions
patterns.howToSpot: The question gives a type of file and asks for its extension.
steps: .pptx is the default since 2007.
.ppt is the old format.
.ppsx opens as a show. .potx is a template. .pptm has macros.
patterns.why: The letters carry the meaning: s is show, t is template, m is macro.

example.q: A PowerPoint file that opens directly in slide show mode has the extension:
steps: It must open as a show.
The s stands for show.

steps: Handouts print 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 slides per page.
Notes Page prints one slide with notes below.

example.q: Which is NOT a valid number of slides per page for a PowerPoint handout: 3, 4, 5 or 6?

Hyperlinks and action buttons also sit there.
Design tab holds themes.

steps: SmartArt is an object added to a slide.
Objects are added on the Insert tab.

subtopics.title: Views, slide master, transitions vs animations
subtopics.concept: PowerPoint shows a presentation in six **views**. **Normal** is the default. A **transition** is how one slide replaces the next. An **animation** moves an object on a slide. Exams often ask you to tell these apart.

tricks.title: Between or within
tricks.body: Transition happens between slides. Animation happens within a slide, on an object.

tricks.title: Four animation kinds
tricks.body: Entrance brings an object in, Emphasis makes it stand out, Exit takes it away, Motion Path moves it along a line.

example.q: An object flies onto the slide when you click. Which animation type is this?
steps: The object is arriving.
Arrival is an Entrance effect.

mistakes.wrong: Calling the effect between slides an animation.
mistakes.right: It is a transition. Animation acts on objects inside a slide.

mistakes.wrong: Using Normal view to reorder many slides.
mistakes.right: Slide Sorter is best for reordering.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Slide Show is the default view.
Putting Transitions on the Animations tab.
mistakes.right: Transitions has its own tab, next to Design.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking a hidden slide is deleted.
mistakes.right: A hidden slide stays in the file and is only skipped in the show.

subtopics.notes:
### The views
Choose a view from the View tab or from the buttons on the status bar.

| View | Use |
|---|---|
| **Normal** | The **default view**. Thumbnails, slide pane and notes pane together |
| **Outline** | Shows only the text of all slides in a list |
| **Slide Sorter** | Shows all slides as small pictures. Best for reordering and deleting |
| **Notes Page** | Shows one slide with its speaker notes |
| **Reading View** | A window-sized show for reading, with a taskbar still visible |
| **Slide Show** | Full-screen show for the audience |

> **Rule:** For "reorder or rearrange slides", the answer is Slide Sorter.

### Other view tools
- **Zoom** enlarges or shrinks the slide on screen.
- **Fit to Window** sizes the slide to fill the pane.
- **Gridlines** and **Guides** help you line up objects.
- **Ruler** shows margins and tab stops.
- **Color, Grayscale and Black and White** show how a deck will print.

### Which view for which job
- Edit one slide in detail: Normal.
- Write or check the flow of text: Outline.
- Move many slides: Slide Sorter.
- Add speaker notes: Notes Page or the Notes pane.
- Run the show: Slide Show.

### Transition vs animation
This pair is a favourite exam trap.

| | Transition | Animation |
|---|---|---|
| Applies to | The **slide** as a whole | An **object** on a slide (text, picture, shape) |
| Happens | **Between** two slides | **Within** a slide |
| Tab | **Transitions** | **Animations** |
| Examples | Fade, Push, Wipe | Fly In, Zoom, Spin |

Animation has four groups.

1. **Entrance:** the object arrives.
2. **Emphasis:** the object stands out while it stays.
3. **Exit:** the object leaves.
4. **Motion Path:** the object moves along a line you draw.

> **Tip:** Entrance is usually green, Emphasis is yellow and Exit is red in the Animation gallery.

### Timing and rehearsal
- **Advance slide** can be On Mouse Click or After a set time.
- **Rehearse Timings** records how long you speak on each slide.
- **Duration** sets how long a transition or animation runs.
- **Animation Pane** lists every animation in order and lets you change the order.
- **Animation Painter** copies an animation to another object.

### Slide Show settings
The Slide Show tab holds **From Beginning**, **From Current Slide**, **Custom Slide Show**, **Set Up Slide Show** and **Hide Slide**. A hidden slide stays in the file but is skipped in the show.

> **Note:** Presenter View shows your notes and the next slide on your screen. The audience sees only the current slide.

patterns.name: Identify the view
patterns.howToSpot: The question describes what the screen shows and asks for the view.
steps: Thumbnails, slide and notes together mean Normal.
Small pictures of all slides mean Slide Sorter.
Only text in a list means Outline.
Full screen for the audience means Slide Show.
patterns.why: Each view has a unique screen layout.

example.q: Which view shows all slides as small pictures, best for rearranging them?
steps: Many small pictures are shown.
That view is for rearranging.
It is Slide Sorter.

patterns.name: Default view
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for the view PowerPoint opens in.
steps: Normal view opens by default.
It mixes thumbnails, slide pane and notes pane.
Slide Show must be started on purpose.
patterns.why: The default view is a fixed fact.

example.q: The default view of MS PowerPoint is:
steps: The view for editing opens first.
It is Normal view.

patterns.name: Transition vs animation
patterns.howToSpot: The question describes an effect and asks whether it is a transition or an animation.
steps: Ask what it applies to: a slide or an object.
Effects between two slides are transitions.
Effects on text or pictures are animations.
patterns.why: Both are motion effects, but they act on different things.

example.q: Fade between Slide 2 and Slide 3 is an example of a:
steps: It happens between slides.
So it is not an animation.
It is a transition.

patterns.name: Animation categories
patterns.howToSpot: The question describes how an object behaves and asks for its category.
steps: Arriving is Entrance.
Standing out while staying is Emphasis.
Leaving is Exit.
Moving along a line is Motion Path.
patterns.why: The four names describe the object's life on the slide.

example.q: Which animation type moves an object along a drawn line?
steps: The path is drawn by the user.
The type is named for the path.

patterns.name: Rehearse timings and hidden slides
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks how to time a talk or how to skip a slide in the show.
steps: Rehearse Timings records the time on each slide.
Hide Slide skips a slide in the show.
Both are on the Slide Show tab.
patterns.why: The Slide Show tab holds the tools for running the talk.

example.q: Which tool records how long you speak on each slide?
steps: It records time while you practise.
It is Rehearse Timings.

Slide Sorter is best for reordering or deleting slides.
Transition is between slides. Animation is on an object within a slide.
Animation types: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Path.
Rehearse Timings records the time spent on each slide.
A hidden slide stays in the file and is skipped in the show.

subtopics.title: Slideshow and editing shortcuts
subtopics.concept: PowerPoint shortcuts fall into two sets: keys used while **editing** and keys used while the **show is running**. **F5** starts the show from the beginning and **Shift+F5** starts it from the current slide. **Esc** ends the show.

tricks.title: Shift means here
tricks.body: F5 starts from the beginning. Add Shift and it starts from the current slide.

example.q: How do you start a show from the slide you are on?
steps: F5 starts from slide 1.
Adding Shift starts from here.

tricks.title: Colour keys
tricks.body: B makes the screen black and W makes it white. Press the same key again to bring the slide back.

tricks.title: New vs duplicate
tricks.body: Ctrl+M adds a fresh slide. Ctrl+D makes a copy of the selected one. Ctrl+N is a whole new presentation.

mistakes.wrong: Using F5 to start from the current slide.
mistakes.right: F5 starts from the beginning. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.
Ctrl+M adds a slide. Ctrl+N makes a new presentation.

mistakes.wrong: Using Esc to open Presenter View.
mistakes.right: Alt+F5 opens Presenter View. Esc ends the show.
B is a black screen. W is a white screen.
In show mode Ctrl+P gives the pen.

subtopics.notes:
### Starting and ending a show
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **F5** | Start the show from the first slide |
| **Shift+F5** | Start the show from the current slide |
| **Alt+F5** | Open Presenter View |
| **Esc** | End the show |

> **Rule:** F5 starts at the beginning. Shift+F5 starts where you are.

### Keys during the show
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **N**, Enter, Space or Right arrow | Next slide |
| **P**, Backspace or Left arrow | Previous slide |
| **B** | Black screen. Press again to return |
| **W** | White screen. Press again to return |
| **Number + Enter** | Jump to that slide number |
| **Ctrl+L** | Laser pointer |
| **Ctrl+P** | Pen |
| **Ctrl+A** | Arrow pointer back |
| **E** | Erase pen drawings |

Typing 5 and pressing Enter jumps to slide 5.

> **Watch:** Ctrl+P prints when you edit. During the show, it gives the pen. The context decides.

### Keys while editing
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+M** | New slide |
| **Ctrl+N** | New presentation |
| **Ctrl+D** | Duplicate the selected slide or object |
| **Ctrl+K** | Insert hyperlink |
| **Ctrl+S** | Save |
| **F12** | Save As |
| **Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y** | Undo / Redo |
| **Ctrl+B / I / U** | Bold, italic, underline |
| **Ctrl+E / L / R / J** | Centre, left, right, justify |
| **Ctrl+A** | Select all |
| **Ctrl+G** | Group selected objects |
| **Ctrl+Shift+G** | Ungroup |

### Presenter View
Presenter View shows the current slide, the next slide, your notes and a timer on your own screen. The audience sees only the slide. It is useful when you use two screens or a projector.

> **Tip:** On a laptop with a projector, Presenter View keeps your notes private.

### Print and save keys
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+P** | Print (in editing mode) |
| **Ctrl+O** | Open a presentation |
| **Ctrl+W** | Close the presentation |
| **Ctrl+F** | Find text |
| **Ctrl+H** | Replace text |

### Extra show-mode keys
- **Home** jumps to the first slide. **End** jumps to the last slide.
- **Ctrl+H** hides the pointer and the buttons at once.
- **S** stops or restarts an automatic show.
- **Right-click** in a show opens a menu with Previous, Next, Go to Slide and End Show.
- **F1** opens the list of show-mode help keys.

> **Note:** During a show, plain letter keys act as commands. That is why B and W do not type letters.

### Quick memory hooks
- B is for black, W is for white.
- N is next, P is previous.
- M is for a new slide.
- The number keys plus Enter work like a jump button.
- Shift adds a twist: F5 starts at the top, Shift+F5 starts here.

patterns.name: Start and end the show
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks how to begin or end a slide show.
steps: F5 starts at the first slide.
Shift+F5 starts at the current slide.
Esc ends the show.
patterns.why: The Shift key means from here.

example.q: The shortcut to start a slide show from the current slide is:
steps: F5 alone starts from slide 1.
The current slide needs Shift.

patterns.name: Keys during the show

steps: B is a black screen and W is white.
N or P moves to next or previous.
A number with Enter jumps to that slide.
patterns.why: Show-mode keys are single letters that hint at the action.

example.q: During a slide show, pressing the B key:
steps: B is the first letter of black.
The screen turns black.

patterns.name: New slide, new presentation, duplicate
patterns.howToSpot: The question asks the key for adding a slide or creating a file.
steps: Ctrl+M adds a slide.
Ctrl+N creates a new presentation.
Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide.
patterns.why: M, N and D are close together, so options swap them.

example.q: Which shortcut inserts a new slide in PowerPoint?
steps: Ctrl+N is a new file.
A new slide uses M.

patterns.name: Pointer tools: laser and pen

steps: Ctrl+L is the laser pointer.
Ctrl+P is the pen.
E erases the drawings.
patterns.why: The letters hint at the tool: L for laser, P for pen.

example.q: Which shortcut turns on the laser pointer during a show?
steps: The laser pointer starts with L.
It uses Ctrl.

patterns.howToSpot: The question asks for the Presenter View key or the hyperlink key.
steps: Alt+F5 opens Presenter View.
Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink.
Presenter View shows notes and the next slide.
patterns.why: These two are asked less often but follow the same rule.

example.q: Presenter View in PowerPoint opens with:
steps: F5 starts the show.
Adding Alt opens Presenter View.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to start the slideshow / start from the current slide / end the show', or during-show keys: next, previous, black screen, jump to a slide number.
pyqPatterns.approach: Fix the row: F5 = full show from slide 1, Shift+F5 = from the current slide, Esc = stop. In the show, N/Enter/Space move ahead, P/Backspace move back, B blacks and W whites the screen, number+Enter jumps. B never means 'back'.

example.q: Which key ends a running PowerPoint slideshow?
example.solution: Esc — F5 and Shift+F5 start shows; Esc leaves the show.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Default extension of a PowerPoint 2007+ file', identification of .ppsx, .ppt or .potx, or odd-one-out among Office extensions.
pyqPatterns.approach: The X/m/t rule again: .pptx default (2007+, X = XML), .ppt = 97-2003, .ppsx = Show that opens already running, .potx = template, .pptm/.ppsm = macro-enabled. In mixed-option lists, the lone X-format beats the three 97-2003 files.

example.q: A file saved as seminar.ppsx opens:
example.solution: Directly as a running slideshow — .ppsx is the PowerPoint Show format.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which view is best to reorder slides?', 'the default view', 'which view prints slide plus notes', or a matched pair with one view on the wrong job.
pyqPatterns.approach: Normal builds (default), Outline strips to text, Slide Sorter reorders thumbnails, Notes Page puts slide above speaker notes, Reading runs a small-window show, Slide Show delivers full screen. 'Rearrange/organise slides' always maps to Slide Sorter.

example.q: To rearrange the slides of a 30-slide deck by dragging, which view is best?
example.solution: Slide Sorter — all slides appear as thumbnails and can be dragged into any order.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The effect when one slide changes to the next' or 'a picture flying in is a ___' — the transition/animation pair with the four animation categories as a variant.
pyqPatterns.approach: Between slides = transition (Fade, Push, Wipe); on objects inside a slide = animation, in four types: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Path. Match the actor in the stem: the slide changes (transition) or an object acts (animation).

example.q: A picture flying into the slide from the left is a(n):
example.solution: Entrance animation — transitions play between slides, animations act on objects.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to insert a new slide' with Ctrl+N planted, or 'Ctrl+M does what?' — plus duplicate-slide questions.
pyqPatterns.approach: Ctrl+M = new slide inside the file; Ctrl+N = new presentation file; Ctrl+D = duplicate the selected slide. The Home tab's New Slide button does Ctrl+M's job with the mouse.

example.q: The shortcut to insert a new slide is:
example.solution: Ctrl+M — Ctrl+N creates a separate new presentation.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A scenario: 'same logo on all slides', 'change fonts of the whole deck', 'ready-made design with sample content' — which feature fits?
pyqPatterns.approach: Slide Master repeats edits on every slide (logo, fonts, background, footer); theme = look only; template = theme + layouts + sample content; layout = placeholder arrangement of one slide type. 'In one step for all slides' points to the master.

example.q: Where should a college logo be placed so that it appears on every slide?
example.solution: On the Slide Master — everything there repeats on all slides based on it.

solvedExamples.q: Which function key starts a slide show from the beginning in MS PowerPoint?
solvedExamples.solution: F5 runs the slideshow from slide 1 (Shift+F5 starts from the current slide). F7 checks spelling, F12 is Save As, F2 has no presentation role.
solvedExamples.shortcut: F5 = Full show from the First slide.

solvedExamples.q: The effect that controls how one slide is replaced by the next slide is called:
solvedExamples.solution: Transitions govern slide-to-slide changeover (Fade, Push, Wipe). Animations act on individual objects inside a slide - entrance, emphasis, exit, motion paths.
solvedExamples.shortcut: 'Between two slides' -> transition; 'within one slide' -> animation.

solvedExamples.q: During a running slide show, pressing the B key:
options: Turns the screen black until pressed again
solvedExamples.solution: B blanks the screen to black (useful while discussing or pausing); pressing B again restores the slide. Esc ends the show, P moves to the previous slide.
solvedExamples.shortcut: B = Blackout, W = Washout. Neither navigates.

solvedExamples.q: In which view can all slides be seen together as thumbnails for easy rearranging?
solvedExamples.solution: Slide Sorter displays the whole deck as miniature slides, making reorder, duplicate and delete operations quick. Normal view edits a single slide's content.
solvedExamples.shortcut: 'See all slides together / rearrange' = Slide Sorter, word for word.

practice.q: The default file extension of a PowerPoint 2019 presentation is:
practice.solution: PowerPoint 2007 onwards saves as .pptx (Office Open XML). .ppt is the 97-2003 format, .potx is a template, .ppsx is a show file.
practice.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+, same rule as docx/xlsx.

practice.q: A file saved as .ppsx:
options: Opens directly as a running slide show
practice.solution: The .ppsx 'PowerPoint show' launches straight into the slideshow when double-clicked; to edit it, open PowerPoint first and browse to the file.

practice.q: The dashed boxes on a slide that hold the title or body text are called:
practice.solution: Placeholders are the pre-formatted containers (title, content, media) defined by the slide layout; text typed into them feeds the Outline view.
practice.shortcut: Presentation-speak: layout defines placeholders; theme defines colours.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts a new slide in the open presentation?
practice.solution: Ctrl+M adds a new slide. Ctrl+N creates a whole new presentation file; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object; Ctrl+S saves.
practice.shortcut: M for More slide; N gives a new FILE, not a slide.

practice.q: Shift+F5 in MS PowerPoint:
options: Starts the show from the currently selected slide
practice.solution: Shift+F5 runs the presentation from the slide you are currently editing - handy while testing a single slide. F5 alone always starts from the first slide.

practice.q: Which key combination ends a running slide show?
practice.solution: Esc exits the slideshow back to the editor (Alt+F4 would close PowerPoint itself; F5 starts a show).
practice.shortcut: Presenting runs until Escape - the universal cancel key.

practice.q: To change the font, colour scheme and logo position on every slide at once, edit the:
practice.solution: The Slide Master is the parent design; changes there cascade to every slide built on its layouts - the standard way to rebrand a deck globally.
practice.shortcut: 'Every slide at once' = Master (slide master for slides, handout master for printouts).

practice.q: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Path are categories of:
practice.solution: These four are animation effect types acting on objects within a slide. Transitions only control slide-to-slide changeover.
practice.shortcut: Object effects = animation (the 4 categories listed); slide changeover = transition.

practice.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker's notes below?
practice.solution: Notes Page view (and its print option) shows the slide above and its notes beneath - used while preparing to speak.
practice.shortcut: Slide on top, notes underneath = Notes Page.

practice.q: The Rehearse Timings feature is used to:
options: Record the time spent on each slide for automatic advance
Time the download of the file
practice.solution: Rehearse Timings records how long each slide stays on screen while you practise, then can auto-advance the show using those durations - essential for self-running kiosks.
practice.shortcut: Practise now, auto-advance later - that is Rehearse Timings.

practice.q: Handouts printed with the '3 slides' layout are popular because:
options: Lines for audience notes appear beside each slide
They include the full speaker notes
practice.solution: The 3-slides-per-page handout prints each slide with ruled lines beside it so the audience can take notes. Speaker notes are NOT included (that is the Notes Pages layout).
practice.shortcut: 3-up = slides + note lines; Notes Pages = slide + your notes.

practice.q: In a running show, which key sequence jumps directly to slide number 7?
practice.solution: Type the slide number and press Enter to jump straight there during a show (works up to the deck's length).
practice.shortcut: Type-and-Enter is the show's hidden navigator; Home/End only reach first/last.

practice.q: Which Office-wide shortcut opens the Font dialog box in PowerPoint?
practice.solution: Ctrl+T opens the Font dialog (face, style, size, effects) in PowerPoint. Ctrl+F is Find; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object.
practice.shortcut: In PPT, T = Type(faces): Ctrl+T is the font box.

practice.q: Presenter View during a slideshow shows the presenter:
options: Only the current slide, like the audience
Current slide, next slide, notes and a timer
practice.solution: Presenter View (Alt+F5, or enabled in Slide Show settings with two displays) gives the speaker the current slide, a peek at the next, speaker notes and a clock/timer, while the audience sees only the slide.
practice.shortcut: Presenter gets a dashboard; audience gets the slide - nothing else.

practice.q: The default file extension of a PowerPoint 2007 or later presentation is —
practice.solution: **.pptx** is the Office Open XML default (X = XML). .ppt is 97-2003, .ppsx is a show, .potx is a template.

practice.q: Double-clicking a .ppsx file in Windows Explorer will —
options: Open it for editing in Normal view
Start playing it as a slideshow
practice.solution: **.ppsx = PowerPoint Show** — it opens running as a show, ready for the audience, not in the editor.

practice.q: Which extension belongs to a PowerPoint template?
practice.solution: **t = template**: .potx (plain) and .potm (with macros).

practice.q: Which option is the odd one out?
practice.solution: .ppt, .doc and .xls are all pre-2007 binary formats; **.pptx** alone is a 2007+ Office Open XML file.

practice.q: Which shortcut key inserts a new slide into the current presentation?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+M = new slide**; Ctrl+N would open a whole new presentation file.

practice.q: Pressing Ctrl+N inside PowerPoint creates —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+N = new presentation** (a separate file). The new slide key is Ctrl+M.

practice.q: A theme in PowerPoint controls —
practice.solution: A **theme is only the look**. A template additionally carries layouts, masters and sample content.

practice.q: Which design choice fixes where the title and content boxes sit on a slide?
practice.solution: A **layout** positions the placeholders (Title Slide, Title and Content, Blank...).

practice.q: A PowerPoint presentation is a collection of —
practice.solution: The presentation file is a sequence of **slides** shown one after another.

practice.q: The one-click buttons inside a content placeholder insert —
options: A table, chart, SmartArt, picture or video
practice.solution: The **content placeholder's icon row** drops any of these objects straight into the box.

practice.q: Free text placed anywhere on a slide needs which tool?
practice.solution: **Insert, Text Box** puts a movable text container anywhere; placeholders stay in their layout positions.

practice.q: Match: 1. Ctrl+M 2. Ctrl+N 3. Ctrl+D — a. new presentation b. duplicate slide c. new slide
practice.solution: Ctrl+M = new slide, Ctrl+N = new presentation, Ctrl+D = duplicate the selected slide.
practice.shortcut: M slide, N file, D duplicate.

practice.q: The default view of PowerPoint while editing is —
practice.solution: **Normal view** shows one large slide with the slides/outline and notes panes around it.

practice.q: Ravi wants to rearrange 30 slides by dragging. The best view is —
practice.solution: **Slide Sorter** shows every slide as a thumbnail, so reordering, copying and deleting take seconds.

practice.q: Which view shows only the text (titles and body) of all slides as a list?
practice.solution: **Outline view** strips graphics and shows the text skeleton — quick for fixing wording and order.

practice.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker notes below it?
practice.solution: **Notes Page** lays out the slide above its notes — designed for the presenter's printout.

practice.q: Changes made on the Slide Master affect —
options: All slides based on that master
practice.solution: The **master drives the design of every slide** that follows it — logo, fonts and background included.

practice.q: Which view should Meena open to insert her institute's name at the bottom of every slide at once?
practice.solution: Footers, logos and page numbers belong on the **Slide Master** — set once, visible everywhere.

practice.q: The effect shown when one slide changes to the next is a —
practice.solution: Slide-to-slide movements (Fade, Push, Wipe) are **transitions**.

practice.q: A picture flying into a slide from the left is an example of —
practice.solution: Effects **on objects** are animations; 'flying in' is an **Entrance** animation. Transitions act between slides.

practice.q: The four categories of PowerPoint animations are —
practice.solution: Animations come in **Entrance** (arrive), **Emphasis** (highlight), **Exit** (leave) and **Motion Path** (move along a line).

practice.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Transitions play between slides; animations play on objects
Animations play between slides; transitions play on objects
Transitions and animations are the same feature
practice.solution: The core distinction: **between slides = transition; inside a slide = animation**.

practice.q: A handout in PowerPoint is —
options: The first slide of a show
A printed sheet with several slide thumbnails per page
practice.solution: **Handouts** print 1-9 slide thumbnails per page for the audience to keep.

practice.q: Where are speaker notes typed so that the audience never sees them on screen?
options: In the notes pane / Notes Page view
practice.solution: Notes live under the slide in **Normal** or in **Notes Page** view — they are projected never.

practice.q: Which key starts a PowerPoint slideshow from the FIRST slide?
practice.solution: **F5 = full show from slide 1.** Shift+F5 starts from the current slide; Esc stops.

practice.q: To rehearse from slide 12 without replaying slides 1-11, press —
practice.solution: **Shift+F5 runs the show from the slide you are on** — a rehearsal time-saver.

practice.q: A running slideshow is closed with —
practice.solution: **Esc exits the show** and returns to Normal editing view.

practice.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Esc — start the show from current slide
practice.solution: F5 starts, Shift+F5 starts from the current slide, Esc stops — the reversed options are all traps.

practice.q: During a slideshow, which key moves to the NEXT slide?
practice.solution: **N = next** (Enter, Space and Page Down also work); P = previous.

practice.q: During a show, the speaker wants the audience to look at him, not the slide. He presses —
options: B to black out the screen
practice.solution: **B blanks the screen to black** (W makes it white); pressing B again restores the slide.

practice.q: To jump directly to slide 15 during a show, press —
practice.solution: **Number + Enter** teleports the show to that slide number.

practice.q: Which key does NOT advance to the next slide during a show?
practice.solution: Space, Enter and Page Down all advance; **B only blacks the screen**.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts a hyperlink in PowerPoint?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+K = hyperlink** in every Office program. Ctrl+M is new slide, Ctrl+H opens Replace.

practice.q: Ctrl+D in PowerPoint duplicates —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+D = duplicate** whatever is selected — a slide, a shape or a picture.

practice.q: Presenter View gives the presenter —
options: Current slide, next slide, notes and a timer
practice.solution: **Presenter View** is the speaker's private dashboard; the projector shows only the slide.

practice.q: Which feature records the time spent on each slide for a self-running show?
practice.solution: **Rehearse Timings** (Slide Show tab) records per-slide seconds so the show can run unattended.
